item.content:encoded:
Old discussion is old.

Anyway, Roland, I think the point Dr. Gears and Unimport were getting at last year was that there's a difference between subtle seeding of reoccurring characters, and articles where the characters really become the focus, not the SCP itself.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Personally, I fear I actually disagree. I like that there's been a growing fleshing-out of the background characters and forces of the Foundation universe. I don't really read the wiki for disconnected, usually depressing creepypasta, but as a shared universe with (subtle) trends and arcs, which I feel is a richer approach.

That said, I think that other comments here may be wise and that splitting the experimentation log into a separate article was a wise decision.

item.title: Re:
item.content:encoded:
Yeah, an E-class! We even forget there are E-Classe personel…

Here's the info:

"E: Temporarily affixed to the start of a security clearance (e.g. E1), this is used when a new SCP object has been discovered but is still in an unsecured or uncontrolled state. E-clearance personnel are tasked with bringing the SCP into effect and maintaining it. Once the SCP are in place and the object is secure, the E is removed and the personnel are given the appropriate number on the end of their clearance."

item.title: Re:
item.content:encoded:
I see where you're coming from.

I know that in Dr. Clef's list of overdone SCP's, he listed SCP's that only make other SCP's, but I originally wrote this with the intention that the stuff SCP-624 made was completely separate from the fact it's a mind-reading mp3 player, which is contain-worthy on its own.

Do you think it would help if I made the test log a separate entity from the SCP entirely, so that the test log would end up in something more along the lines of the Foundation Tales and SCP-624 would be an interesting thing on its own? Plus, people could rate the SCP on its own merrits and the results themselves in their own rights that way.

item.title: Re:
item.content:encoded:
I think we're just losing sight of the idea that the Foundation is a massive place, and individual researchers shouldn't keep cropping up to the extent that they do, unless they're really, really important individuals.

Well, that's the perspective I have on it. Maybe I've got the whole thing reversed, maybe I'm not seeing it in the same way everyone else does.

item.title: Re:
item.content:encoded: I'm not trying to call you on your shit here, mind you. Just saying there's nothing wrong with "wouldn't it be cool if…" when it works, and I for one think it works here (as it does on 914).

item.title: Re:
item.content:encoded:
Honestly, i didn't initially intend for SCP-914 to become as big and inter-connected as it is. I initially thought it was too close to 882 and would be quickly voted down. I think it can still stand on it's own, even if the extended log entry were removed. The section that links to the extended test was originally not there, and I've debated removing it a few times. Plus, the entry itself pre-dates many of the staff here…

Still, i admit i fall into the raving fanboy trap at times as well. I've tried to keep most of my SCP entries as stand-alone as possible, but i admit i succumb to "wouldn't it be cool if…" at times.

item.title: Re:
item.content:encoded: I respectfully submit that this, coming from the man who created SCP-914, is more than a mite hypocritical.

item.title: Re:
item.content:encoded:
MrUnimport, you have surmised, in one short paragraph, the entire point i was trying to make, and a salute you.

The staff should be a background thing, like the Cthulhu Mythos was originally started: a cosmic, semi in-joke between multiple authors, which could be followed or expanded on by those who tried to look for it, or go wholly unnoticed. Reading "The Shadow over Innsmouth" with a good understanding of the Cthulhu mythos lets you see a lot of inter-connected ideas…but it can be read on it's own, with no foreknowledge, and still be a solid horror story.

I guess I've always looked at the staff as the "Mythos" of the SCP…the background "in joke" that bubbles up from time to time. That's not to say that they have no place in a starring role (see the Wanderlust series), just not in the main SCP articles as much.

item.title: Re:
item.content:encoded:
Yes, I agree. I think there's been a recent overemphasis on the characters we've set up, to the detriment of the SCPs themselves and the greater Foundation, which continues to lurk in the dark behind the wacky antics of our top researchers.

But hey, I haven't contributed one yet, and my opinion counts for nothing.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
while the idea is neat, it still seems like a item who's sole purpose is to be used by the senior staff to interesting effect. As a stand-alone concept, without the addition of the staff tests, it's somewhat interesting, but not as strong. Anything that uses other SCP items, Site Staff, or other aspects of the larger "SCP Universe" can suffer for it, if not done well. Each SCP entry should, in my opinion, be a stand-alone concept, and not need a lot of "background knowledge" to understand.

It's not a bad idea, but i just feel it's too reliant on backstory. Just a personal preference i guess…
